historical_references.reference: Saint Kenelm, a young prince of Mercia, was the son of King Wulfhere and Aetheldred, daughter of King Penda of Northumbria. He is said to have lived in the early eighth century. Kenelm was born in Hereford and was raised in the monastery of Evesham. According to legend, he was hidden in a cave at Evesham during a Danish invasion, where he remained for many years. Eventually, he was discovered and restored to his throne.

Another account suggests that Saint Kenelm was a 12th-century noble of Gloucestershire. He was the son of a wealthy family and was known for his generosity and piety. He is said to have lived in the late 1100s and early 1200s. According to legend, Kenelm was murdered by his stepmother and buried in the church of St. Peter and St. Paul at Northleach, where he was later venerated as a saint.
